conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Lee. You were brought in this morning because of vomiting. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I woke up at 4 a.m. with sudden nausea and started vomiting. I’ve done it about 10 times since then. It’s just like my last episode.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Was there any blood in the vomit?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not really blood, but there was some dark, coffee-ground-looking stuff in it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. That can happen with stomach irritation. You had a Botox injection in your esophagus a week ago, right? And your gastric pacer was adjusted?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. I felt better for a few days, then this hit me out of nowhere.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s consistent with your gastroparesis flaring up again. We’ll keep you here because you can’t keep anything down. We’ve started IV fluids and anti-nausea meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be able to eat soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We need to let your stomach rest. Once the vomiting stops, we’ll try small sips, then advance slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an X-ray of your abdomen to check for a blockage. Good news — there’s no obstruction. Your gastric pacer is in place and looks stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not broken?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s working fine. This is more about your stomach not moving food properly, which is part of your diabetes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood pressure was high this morning, likely from pain and vomiting. We gave you a medication to bring it down, and it’s improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had high blood pressure before. Is it a concern?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re watching it. We’ll switch you to your usual blood pressure pill tomorrow if it stays under control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I take lisinopril at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart that. Your diabetes is also being managed with your usual insulin — glargine at night and sliding scale for meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still nauseous, but not vomiting as much. The IV meds are helping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s progress. We’ll keep the IV fluids going and monitor your labs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your white blood cell count was a bit high yesterday, but it’s coming down. That’s a sign your body isn’t fighting a serious infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had a urine test — was there an infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The culture showed mixed bacteria, but it looks like contamination from skin. No treatment needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. I was worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to try giving you small sips of water. If you keep that down, we can move to clear liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great! I’m ready to try.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well overnight — no vomiting. We’re advancing you to a soft diet. Start with small bites and chew well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We want to make sure you can keep food and your medications down for a full day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood sugar has been stable on your home insulin plan. The endocrine team reviewed and agrees it’s appropriate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I don’t want to change my routine if it’s working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did another abdominal X-ray yesterday to check for ileus. It was clear — no blockage or slow transit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So my stomach is just slow, not blocked?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That’s gastroparesis. We’re adding metoclopramide — Reglan — to help speed things up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve taken that before. Does it have side effects?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sometimes it can cause restlessness, but we’ll start low and watch you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. You’re eating soft food, keeping meds down, and not vomiting. We’re planning for discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful! What about my medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home with your insulin, plus new prescriptions: Reglan for stomach emptying, Protonix for acid reflux, Zofran for nausea as needed, and lisinopril for blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll take them as directed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One thing — your sodium level is low, 130. But you’re not having symptoms like dizziness, so it’s mild.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I worry?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. But if you feel lightheaded or confused, seek care. We want you to get a blood test next week to check it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. You can go home today. Make sure to follow up with your gastroenterologist — they may check your gastric pacer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I have an appointment scheduled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Take your new meds, stay hydrated, and call if nausea returns or you feel unwell.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing — your discharge papers say to draw labs next week. Please call your PCP with the results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re finalizing your discharge. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I understand everything. Thanks for your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care and get some rest at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming — you’ve tolerated breakfast and your pills. You’re cleared to leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Here’s your prescription list and lab slip. Please follow up as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you only if you need us.
